mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 5.5% signals monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a strong labor market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 30% of cases when UNRATE is below 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 2000 units signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of cases when HOUST is above 2000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 30% of cases when both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 115 signals strong supply-side activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO exceeds 115, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 4.5% signals monetary easing, which stimulates economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 30% of cases when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong demand-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of cases when both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals inflationary pressures, which may lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 30% of cases when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.
